title: What rule makes the savings in Meera's box grow?
description: Meera counts the rupees in her savings box each month. The video finds how much each count grows and carries the row on three more months.
teaching_notes: One idea: find how much every jump adds; if it is the same each time, that is the rule. Watch for children who take the first number as the rule.

source: Find the rule and write the next three numbers: 2,000, 2,500
video_script.why: The child can read big numbers but has not yet found the amount that a row of numbers grows by.
video_script.substitution: Take away each number from the next one; the same answer every time is the rule, and adding it to the last number gives the next ones.
video_script.anchor: Meera's savings box at home in Pune, counted at the end of each month
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu takes the first number two thousand as the amount added. The first jump is only five hundred, so the rule cannot be two thousand.
video_script.payoff_line: the rule is add five hundred

final_answer.value: The rule is add 500; the next numbers are 4,000, 4,500 and 5,000
final_answer.spoken: add five hundred, then four thousand, four thousand five hundred and five thousand

maths_rules: the jump is 500 every time, so the rule is add 500
slip: the rule 'add 2,000' would give 2,000 + 2,000 = 4,000 for the second count, but the second count is 2,500
video_script.design: One idea: the same jump every time is the rule. Wrong idea: the first number is the rule. The row of counts sits on the stage with an arrow between each pair; the jump labels arrive in the idea part.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>Meera keeps a savings box at home in Pune. Each month she counts the rupees inside.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>Her counts are two thousand, two thousand five hundred, three thousand and three thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Find the rule and write the next three numbers.

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: the four counts sit in a row; an arrow joins each count to the next; each arrow has an empty label

marks.row: the four counts sit in a row with arrows between them
marks.ask: an empty label appears on every arrow

narration: <bookmark mark='row'/>Look at the row of counts. Each count is joined to the next by an arrow.
<bookmark mark='jump'/>Each arrow is one jump from one month to the next.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>For every jump, ask one thing. How many rupees did the box gain?

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows add 2,000; the first arrow is stretched between 2,000 and 2,500 and looks small; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.first: the first arrow is stretched between 2,000 and 2,500
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>The rule is add two thousand, because the row starts at two thousand.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Look at the first jump. It goes from two thousand to two thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That jump is small, much smaller than two thousand.

beats.on_screen: each arrow gets its label +500; the board reads 2,500 − 2,000 = 500, 3,000 − 2,500 = 500, 3,500 − 3,000 = 500; the rule card reads add 500

marks.take: the board opens with the words smaller count taken from larger
marks.rule: the rule card reading add 500 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Take away the smaller count from the larger one.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Two thousand five hundred take away two thousand leaves five hundred.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Three thousand take away two thousand five hundred leaves five hundred.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Three thousand five hundred take away three thousand leaves five hundred.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Every jump is the same, so the rule is add five hundred.

beats.on_screen: from the last count 3,500 three new boxes fill in turn: 4,000, 4,500, 5,000; the answer card lists them

marks.one: the first empty box fills with 4,000
marks.two: the second empty box fills with 4,500
marks.three: the third empty box fills with 5,000

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>Start from the last count, three thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Add five hundred to reach four thousand.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Add five hundred again to reach four thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Add five hundred once more to reach five thousand.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The next three numbers are four thousand, four thousand five hundred and five thousand.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the savings box; two lines appear: see how much each number grows; the same jump every time is the rule; then a new row 6,000, 6,300, 6,600 and three empty boxes

marks.one: the line see how much each number grows appears
marks.two: the line the same jump every time is the rule appears
marks.turn: a new row 6,000, 6,300, 6,600 appears with three empty boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>To find a rule, see how much each number grows.
<bookmark mark='two'/>If every jump is the same, that jump is the rule.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>Your turn. A row goes six thousand, six thousand three hundred, six thousand six hundred. What is the rule, and what are the next three numbers?
